author: Valerie Anne
title: Liv Hewson Opens Up to Drew Barrymore About the Early Parts of Their Career
content:
feature image photo by The Drew Barrymore Show/Ash Bean via Getty Images

Yellowjackets star Liv Hewson reunited with their former Santa Clarita Diet co-star Drew Barrymore on Drew’s talk show this week.

In the interview, they discuss all sorts of topics, including but not limited to Yellowjackets, of course. Drew presents Liv with gifts for what she thought was their engagement, but Liv reveals that actually they got married already. (There are actually really cute pics that pop up behind them of the couple as well in the clip, so you should check it out.) Drew’s now-wedding gifts are two beautiful candlesticks Drew said represents the two of them living together in harmony.

Liv talks about meeting their now-spouse on the set of Yellowjackets when they were AD, and recounts seeing them for the first time and having a “who IS that” moment immediately.

Drew shows Liv a clip of another of their Santa Clarita Diet co-stars, Skyler Gisondo, asking Liv to share dating advice, and their advice boils down to the fact that people want to feel safe and that should be a priority in any relationship, not just romantic. author: Valerie Anne
title: LGBTQ+ Representation in Television Hits Devastating Lows
content:
As I’m sure you’ve noticed, LGBTQ+ representation in media is at the lowest it’s been in over a decade.

GLAAD’s latest Where We Are in TV study showed some bleak results that reflect the state of the country due to the hateful administration we live under and the wealthy conservatives who own most of the media conglomerates. Trans representation took the biggest hit, going from 33 characters to a measly SEVEN, and since three of them were on shows that were cancelled and four are from limited series, none of those seven will be returning next season. NONE. Devastating.

Twenty-five percent of LGBTQ+ characters have left our screens since last year, which brings the stats to their lowest point in over a decade. Cable television hit a 16-year low. BLEAK.

Streamers have more queer representation than cable and broadcast characters put together, but we have lost almost 100 characters from streamers as well, so even that isn’t great news. And combining streaming, cable, and broadcast, of all LGBTQ+ characters, 44% of them are characters of color, which is the lowest percentage since GLAAD’s 2017-2018 report.

Pride points out that it seems wild to imagine because some of the buzziest shows of the last few years feature queer characters: The Hunting Wives, Hazbin Hotel, Pluribus, Stranger Things, Heated Rivalry. I don’t think this show made it into the count, but we also have Sterling Point and now The Body. Queer people show up for shows that feature them, and queer people are great at telling unique stories. Alas, too many higher-ups lean on outdated Christian ideals and won’t invest in us in an effort to silence us.

This is especially wild because, while it reflects what the political times want you to believe (that queer people are outsiders, among other things), it doesn’t reflect the actual statistics. Every generation reports identifying as gayer than the last, so representation should also be at a steady increase to reflect reality, not a drastic decrease.

The actual numbers of LGBTQ+ characters on broadcast and cable shows are harrowing to look at. There are dozens of characters on any given TV show, and dozens of shows on each network, and yet the highest number among them is HBO with 15 characters. The second-highest is a big drop down, with Fox and Starz coming in with 10 characters each.

The numbers start off a little more promising for streaming, with 116 on Netflix, but then they also start dropping dramatically, with 68 on Prime Video and then again a steep drop to Hulu with 24.

I’m sure you, like I have, felt the shift even before you saw these numbers. Here at Autostraddle, we used to have to have a weekly TV roundup because there were so many queer characters on cable and broadcast shows that we couldn’t keep up with individual recaps. We used to do Pop Culture Fix twice a week to keep up with the news coming at us from all angles. And now there aren’t enough recurring characters for a weekly roundup and barely enough news for 10-15 links a week in a pop culture roundup.

It’s disheartening to see these numbers go down more and more every year when we were in such a steady incline for so long, but the fact is: We’re still here. We’re still out here writing well-rounded characters and telling our stories and watching and supporting the LGBTQ+ characters we DO still have on TV. We will not go quietly into the night. We will keep shouting and keep showing up for the queer shows doing it right until these numbers make sense again.

author: Valerie Anne
title: You Oughta Know That Alanis Morissette Is Pansexual
content:
feature image photo by Credit: NBC / Contributor via Getty Images

It’s official: 90s icon and present-day superstar Alanis Morissette is pansexual. The singer was a guest on the Handsome podcast, which is co-hosted by queer comedians Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin, and they were talking about Alanis’s penchant for a post-breakup rage anthem. Fortune Feimster jokingly asked her, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?” to which Alanis replied, “I’m pansexual, so yeah.”

The energy in the room was perfect. At first, everyone thought it was a joke (or perhaps that she was being…ironic), but when they clarified that Alanis was serious, they all joked that she should have led with that. You walk into a queer podcast with the queer announcement!!

Granted, this is not the first time Alanis has said she isn’t straight. She has been talking about exploring her sexuality and being attracted to women as far back as 2008, and it was apparently at least partly her idea for her character to kiss Sarah Jessica Parker’s Carrie during her Sex and the City guest spot. It’s just the first time she’s used a specific label out loud.

I considered riddling this intro with Alanis-related puns (like the joke my friend made: she’s got one pan in her pocket…) but I’ll save you the cringe. I’ll just say this news has made me even more head over feet for her.

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘Criminal Minds’ Has Unceremoniously Been Canceled
content:
In devastating news for me specifically, it was announced that the upcoming 20th season of Criminal Minds will be its last. What’s worse is that they had already finished filming the series by the time this news broke, and this abrupt cancellation means we won’t even get a proper series finale, even though there will have been over 370 episodes by the time the new season finishes airing. It feels like a slap in the face this show doesn’t deserve!

Now, there’s always the chance another network saves them from oblivion; it’s happened once before. The first 15 seasons of the show aired on CBS from 2005-2020, but then two years later it was revived as Criminal Minds: Evolution on Paramount+ without much structural change. We still had most of the same characters, only now they could say “fuck”, which they did with much aplomb. It is also in this Evolution series that Nicole Pacent joined the show as Rebecca Wilson, who became a love interest for long-standing member of the BAU family Tara Lewis, played by Aisha Tyler.

The shortening from 22 episodes to 10 was a hard one to bear, but I was grateful for anything after that two-year dark period. The bonus gayness didn’t hurt. Unfortunately, this did lead to some disappointing side effects, like the fact that Tara and Rebecca got married entirely off-screen between seasons. author: Audrey Black
title: Dallas Gayborhood Fights Back Against Removal of Rainbow Crosswalks
content:
For years, rainbow crosswalks marked each end of Cedar Springs Road, the iconic strip in Oak Lawn, Dallas’s beloved gayborhood.

As a native Texan, I vividly remember the first time I saw Oak Lawn’s rainbow crosswalks. I was excited to see such a visible sign of belonging and it led me to learn more about Dallas’ rich LGBTQ+ history. I immediately felt welcome and spent more and more time in Oak Lawn as the years passed.

“[The crosswalks] meant inclusion, acceptance, diversity,” David Fisher, an Oak Lawn resident and election judge at the Oak Lawn Branch Library, told me. They communicated that, “this is a neighborhood that’s accepting, and people should feel … comfortable, and like they belong.”

“They almost served as a demarcation point of the Cedar Springs corridor, the neighborhood, of like, ‘This is our street,’” Lee Daugherty, owner of the long-standing gay bar Alexandre’s on Cedar Springs and an active member of the Cedar Springs Merchant Association, told me. “We have long historical ties and cultural ties to this area and to the street. It was a recognition of those who came before, the work they did, the struggle they had, and the continued struggle we have going forward.”
